mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 experiences positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods after UNRATE exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates coupled with falling unemployment indicate a tightening labor market and potential monetary policy constraints, leading to negative equity returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows despite rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the federal funds rate during a tightening cycle may lead to decreased corporate earnings and negative equity returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 experiences positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods following a 0.5% FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which may boost corporate revenues and lead to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following RSAFS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A high industrial production index (INDPRO) suggests strong economic activity, which may lead to positive equity returns as corporate productivity increases.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 experiences negative returns in more than 50% of the 60-day periods after INDPRO surpasses 100.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) accompanied by high inflation (CPIAUCSL) may lead to negative equity returns due to potential interest rate hikes and reduced consumer purchasing power.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows despite strong GDP and high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) in a late-cycle expansion may lead to negative equity returns as the Federal Reserve may tighten monetary policy to control inflation.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 experiences positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following a 0.5% CPIAUCSL increase.
